newsitem.title: USA: NBA-HOW SICK WAS MICHAEL JORDAN?.
newsitem.headline: NBA-HOW SICK WAS MICHAEL JORDAN?.

text.p: So how sick was Michael Jordan?
"He didn't look sick dropping 38 (points)," said Bryon Russell, the Utah Jazz's main defender against Jordan during the Chicago Bulls' 90-88 win in Game 5 of the NBA Finals.
"You guys (reporters) keep on saying he was sick, but he sure didn't look sick."
Indeed none of the Jazz knew Jordan was ill during the game.

But his teammates knew that Jordan, who along with his 38 points had seven rebounds, five assists, three steals and a blocked shot, could hardly stand up. He was suffering from a viral infection that kept him up all night vomiting and in bed all day, unable to eat.
"I've played many seasons with Michael and I've never seen him as sick, to the point where I didn't even think he was going to be able to put his uniform on," said Scottie Pippen.
"And the effort that he came out and gave us today was just incredible. The leadership. He just kept everybody patient and he just made big shots after big shots and he just kept wanting the ball.

"And somehow he just showed how big a professional he is by gutting this game out and staying in there," Pippen continued. "He was dehydrated, felt like he was going to pass out. (They were) feeding him fluids and cold towels and things of that nature.
"But he just really came out and gave us the performance that we needed. There's nothing else to say. He's the greatest, and he's definitely the MVP in my eyes," Pippen said.
Jordan said it was, "all about desire. I wanted it really bad."
"I feel better that we won," added Jordan, who almost single-handedly gave the Bulls a 3-2 lead in the Finals, one victory away from their fifth championship in seven years.
"I endured and it went to a good cause and we won. Now we want to go home and accomplish what we want to accomplish and get one win."
Jordan said the illness had hit at about 3:30 in the morning. "It was just a viral infection," he said.

At first during the game, he said, he felt, "very queasy, low on energy. Once I got out there and started sweating, I was out there and I really didn't want to sit down. I knew I had to play in spurts, with bursts of energy, and then rest for two minutes and do what I have to do."
In the third quarter he said he felt close to passing out.
"I came in at halftime and my energy level was really low. I ate some apple sauce and some sports gel and drank a lot of juices.
"Third quarter, I really felt like I couldn't really catch my wind and I couldn't get my energy level up," he said.
But Jordan still managed to score 15 of his points in the final period and hit the big 3-pointer that proved just barely high enough an obstacle for the Jazz to overcome.
"In the fourth quarter, I don't know how I got through that," Jordan recalled. "I was just trying to gut myself through it."
In the last minute of the two-point victory, he said, "the focus was just to make things happen. Once I got in the act, I didn't have time to think about it. It was more or less instincts."
The Bulls are still worried that he might not recover 100 percent by Game 6 Friday in Chicago.
"It's obvious it's still a concern," said coach Phil Jackson. "I doubt very highly that he'll be here to speak to you tonight."
Jordan did not speak to reporters, but answered questions posed by an NBA official and the league delivered his answers in written form.
"He's dehydrated. He hadn't eaten all day. And he's in a pretty weak state right now. So we'll just have to take what we can take out of this," Jackson said.
The coach said the players who needed it would take Thursday as a "personal heath day ... and hopefully come back on Friday with a renewed energy to win."
